trajectory_summary: This is a short qualification call that surfaces a hard DQ almost immediately: the customer already has a broken existing solar system from SolarCity, not a new-install prospect. The rep handled the disclosure honestly (correctly telling the customer Ion can't service the existing system) and made one legitimate attempt to redirect to a battery/panel add-on sale before the customer declined and the call ended. Given the caveat below, the overall shape is closer to stagnant-to-honest-DQ than a coaching failure.
outcome_dispute: This should be tagged dq, not booked/tentative/callback — the customer has an existing, non-working SolarCity system (orphaned_flow scenario), which is a hard DQ per dq_rules.sunrun_existing/pink_solar_existing analog (SolarCity not listed explicitly but existing_system_broken is an explicit hard DQ), and the call ends with a clear decline and no next step.

observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer has an existing, broken solar system installed by SolarCity (a named hard-DQ company in dq_rules), Ion cannot service it, and the customer declines the only offered alternative (battery/additional panels) — the call ends with no appointment and no next step.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reaches the bill_amount verify step — it is diverted into the orphaned-flow branch as soon as existing panels are spotted on Google Maps, and ends in a DQ/decline before any bill discussion could occur.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: No utility bill was ever raised; the call terminated at the orphaned-flow DQ point before reaching bill collection.
